articleTitle: Chip Design of Low-Phase Noise Colpitts Voltage Controlled Oscillator with Folded-Mirror Mixer
abstract: This article presents a low phase noise voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) adopting optimization colpitts with gm boosting techniques. The excellent performance of the VCO core adopts a phase noise of −123.4 dBc/Hz at 1MHz offset frequency and output power of −6.67dBm from a 5.73 GHz carrier with a 4.7mW power consumption, achieving in an excellent FOM of −191.84 dBc/Hz and displayed by FOMT of −194.61 dBc/Hz. The proposed folded-current mirror mixer produces a conversion power gain of −3 ∼ 0.8 dB, input P1dB of −6 ∼ −4 dBm, IIP3 of −1.4 ∼ 1.8 dBm, LO-RF isolation of 30 dB, respectively. The overall prototypes of colpitts oscillators with folded-current mirror mixer have been fabricated in tsmc <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{0.18}\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS 1P6M process and implemented from supply voltage of 1V.

articleTitle: Towards Broadband D-Band Wireless Communication Systems using Beam Steering in SiGe BiCMOS Technology
abstract: This paper provides an overview of key challenges and solutions for integrated circuits and system-integration in order to realize practical mm-wave wireless communication systems in D-band targeting data rates in the order of 100 Gbps with beam steering functionality. As key element for beam-controlled systems, the design and measurement results of a broadband, low power and digitally adjustable D-band phase shifter are presented. Additionally, system performance limits in different beam-steering architectures are derived. The presented vector modulator core exploits passive phase generation with synthesized high performance couplers, achieving a 360° phase control at a maximum power consumption of 25mW from a 2.5V supply and a maximum 3 dB bandwidth of 20 GHz. Because of its flat gain response and high control-resolution, the phase shifter can be operated within multiple multi-GHz sub-bands within the D-band.

articleTitle: New Development of Electromagnetic Compatibility in the Future: Cognitive Electromagnetic Environment Adaptation
abstract: With the increasing complexity of electromagnetic environment, the problem that radio frequency and electronic equipment could not adapt to the complex electromagnetic environment became more and more prominent. In view of the shortcomings of current methods to help equipment to against more and more electromagnetic interference(EMI), the booming artificial intelligence method was appropriately introduced into the anti-interference design of device, and the concept of cognitive electromagnetic environment adaptation(CEEA) was put forward. The purpose of CEEA was to establish an intelligent and autonomous system capable of perceiving its environment, interpreting it, making suited decisions, and reacting according to the constraints related to the electromagnetic environment. Here summarized the background and related technologies of CEEA, and at the same time clarified the theoretical system and method framework.

articleTitle: 58-GHz Up-Conversion Mixer Using Capacitive Cross-Coupling Neutralization in 180-nm CMOS Technology
abstract: In the millimeter-wave band, the parasitic capacitances of MOSFETs cause degradation of the frequency bandwidth and the conversion gain of an up-conversion mixer. To improve the performance of an up-conversion mixer, we presents an up-conversion mixer with cross-coupled capacitors adopted in the local-oscillator (LO) input ports The cross-coupled capacitors cancel out the gate-to-drain capacitances of nMOSFETs for the LO input. It is verified by simulations that the bandwidth and the conversion gain are improved. The proposed mixer is fabricated by using a 180-nm CMOS process. It is shown that the proposed mixer has the −3 dB bandwidth of 5.9 GHz and the conversion gain of −8.2 dB. This work demonstrates the possibility of realizing 60-GHz transceivers in a mature, low-cost process.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation in the Range of GHz of Integrated Circuit Package with Heat Sink
abstract: With the increase of operating frequency of electronic devices, electromagnetic interference (EMI) radiation in the 20 GHz and higher frequency is becoming an increasingly difficult problem to solve, especially in the integrated circuit (IC) package with heat sink where the radiation from the chip will leak out through the gap between the heat sink and the ground plane of PCB. In this paper, the electromagnetic radiation mechanism of the package with heat sink in the frequency range up to 40 GHz is proposed from plenty of full-wave simulations using different absorbing materials, which is beneficial to the selection of package structural parameters and the suppression of radiation. According to the proposed mechanism, the methods to improve the EMI radiation suppression effect in the frequency range from 20 GHz to 30 GHz are designed.

articleTitle: A Circularly-Polarized-Reconfigurable Dense Dielectric Patch Antenna with Liquid Dielectric
abstract: In this paper, we present a circularly-polarized-reconfigurable dense dielectric (DD) patch antenna. Reconfigurability is adjusted by the liquid dielectric which called the ethyl acetate. When the uniformity of substrate of the DD patch antenna is destroyed by the ethyl acetate, then the proposed DD patch antenna would radiate circularly polarization (CP). In this way, by injecting ethyl acetate into each channel in the substrate, the left-hand polarization (LHCP) and right-hand polarization (RHCP) of the DD patch antenna can be switched.

articleTitle: Fast Prediction for Electromagnetic Shielding Effectiveness of Ground-Via Distribution of SiP by Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: Ground vias are often used as an essential shielding structure in System-in-Package (SiP) to suppress electromagnetic leakage. In this paper, a new method based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is adopted to predict the shielding effectiveness of ground-via distributions. In particular, the suitability of the pooling layer is studied separately. Furthermore, the appropriateness of using the convolutional layer is proved by a comparative experiment with a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model. The method proposed in this paper shows good accuracy in electromagnetic leakage prediction and has universal value in similar prediction tasks. Compared with traditional analysis methods, the proposed CNN model has a significant time advantage, making it possible to use other optimization algorithms to replace the artificial shielding structure design.

articleTitle: A Simple De-embedding Methodology for BGA Transition up to 40GHz
abstract: This paper presents the RF characteristics of ball grid array (BGA) transition with a frequency range from 100MHz to 40GHz. This study mainly introduces the simplest 2-lines de-embedding methodology to analyze the RF properties of BGA transition and transmission line (TL) from the vertical interconnection structure. The S-parameters, derived from the simulation with the 2-lines de-embedding algorithm and simulation directly based on a model in HFSS software, act a consistent trend. In addition, different pitches between signal BGA and ground BGA of vertical interconnection structures were analyzed to figure out the impact on the RF characteristics of BGA transition. According to the result, 2-lines de-embedding method is an excellent fit to achieve the RF property for the vertical interconnection structures.

articleTitle: Coaxial-to-Microstrip Transition for 5G Millimeter Wave Communication Band
abstract: This paper presents a coaxial-to-microstrip transition with improved transmission characteristics for use in 5G millimeter wave communication band. When a coaxial cable and a microstrip line are connected, a discontinuous portion exists at the connection, and the reflection, transmission, and radiation of the incident electromagnetic waves occur due to the discontinuity. To prevent degradation of the transition characteristics due to the discontinuity, metal legs in the coaxial cable are introduced. The proposed coaxial-to-microstrip transition has a higher transmission coefficient than conventional coaxial-to-microstrip transitions.

articleTitle: Antenna Planar Near-Field Measurement System Using Robotics
abstract: An antenna planar near-field measurement system using robotics which is built by BIRMM (Beijing Institute of Radio Metrology and Measurement) is introduced in the paper. The system is consisted of six axis robotic arm, transmitting antenna setup, the vector network analyzer, the AUT (antenna under test) and a scanning probe antenna. The Probe in system is used to collect amplitude and phase of every sampling points on scanning planar. The robotic arm moves according to planar near-field scanning trajectory with the scope of the scanning plane <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{1.6}\ \mathrm{m} \times \mathrm{1.6}\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> and the repetitive positioning accuracy 0.05 mm. Using a 26.5 GHz-40 GHz standard gain horn antenna as the AUT, measurement results of radiation pattern in the system is in good agreement with those in a far-field antenna system. Therefore the antenna planar near-field measurement system has a good performance for 26.5GHz-40GHz antenna measurement

articleTitle: Coverage of Sub-Terahertz Communications and A 300-GHz-Band CMOS Transceiver
abstract: A 44 GHz frequency band from 252 GHz to 296 GHz has been identified for communications in WRC 2019. This frequency band will be the 300 GHz band, which is expected to provide transmission rates in excess of 100 Gb/s for 6G. In this paper, the requirements for ultra-wideband wireless communications in the sub-THz band, including the 300 GHz band, is discussed and present a 300 GHz CMOS wireless transceiver capable of transmitting data rates up to 80 Gb/s.

articleTitle: A Power Divider with High Isolation Based on Microstrip Branching Lines for Ka-Band Transceiver Applications
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band power divider with microstrip branching lines (MBLs) based on a dielectric substrate (RT/duroid 5880 with a thickness of 0.254 mm, permittivity of 2.2, and loss tangent of 0.0009). The proposed power divider consists of two microstrip branching lines and a thin-film resistor of 100 ohm connected to the microstrip branching lines, which leads to high isolation and matching between the two output ports of this power divider. This designed power divider is fabricated and measured. Both simulated and measured results agree well with each other, and show that the insertion loss is less than 4.0 dB, the return loss is higher than 19 dB, and the isolation between the two output ports is higher than 30 dB in the band from 35 - 40 GHz.

articleTitle: K/Ka Slotted Stacked Patch Antenna and Active Array Antenna Design for a 5G/6G Satellite Mobile Communication System
abstract: In this paper, K/Ka TX/RX antenna system which consists of two antennas is designed to form beam steering patterns for transmitter and receiver of a 6G system. After calculating link budget, it is revealed that each antenna needs to have a 64×64 array. In addition, the antennas prepare a 3 dimensional electronically scanning radiation pattern in two different K/Ka frequency bands. The specifications of the receiver/transmitter antenna systems are: frequency: 17.5GHz ~21.5GHz/27.5GHz~31.5GHz; Gain > 35 dB; SWR: <; 3; 3D scanning angles: φ = 360; θ = ±30 (up to ±60 with VIAs/more isolations among antenna elements). For verification, an 8×8 sub-array is designed, simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Comparing of Electromagnetic Shielding Structures for SCPW Transmission Line at 5G FR2 Band
abstract: With the development of 5G millimeter wave and related technologies, working frequency of transmission lines becomes higher and higher, and the high-frequency electromagnetic radiation is a key factor affecting the working of integrated circuits. Therefore, the method to suppress electromagnetic radiation of high-frequency transmission line has become a research hotspot. Two shielding methods are proposed for a flexible segmented coplanar waveguide (SCPW) transmission line at 5G FR2 band (24.25-52.6 GHz) in this paper, adding copper film or adding copper film and metal vias. Through simulation and optimization of CST, results show that adding copper film can effectively suppress electromagnetic radiation of the SCPW transmission line in available frequency band, the shielding effectiveness of one-unit transmission line can reach 10-25 dB, while that of three-unit transmission line is 35-45 dB. On this basis, punching copper vias can further enhance the electromagnetic radiation suppression capability, the shielding effectiveness of one-unit transmission line can reach 50-60 dB, while that of three-unit transmission line is 50-65 dB. However, copper film will weaken the transmission performance, and metal vias will further affect that of SCPW transmission line. In addition, considering that metal vias will make the processing of transmission lines more difficult, if the shielding effectiveness of transmission lines shielded by copper film meets the requirements, it is not recommended to punch metal vias.

articleTitle: Implementation of Millimetre Wave Receiver for Radar Detection and Image Fusion on Embedded Vehicle
abstract: The proposed article presents integrated millimeter wave receiver with hybrid beamforming of radar detection with neural network, optimized power dissipation and enhance performance. The embedded platform of vehicle adopts edge computing vision and deep learning for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). Implementation of millimetre wave receiver of radar detection promoted to decrease image computation with featured object and excellent throughput with parallel achieving in multiple convolutional layers of ARM Neon to comparison with MobileNet and training of deep neural network.

articleTitle: Direct-detection Single-photon Radar at Terahertz Frequencies
abstract: Terahertz single-photon radar is an emerging technology in recent years, which can be exploited to detect ultra-low target echo due to its high sensitivity. In this paper, the single-photon radar equation is derived to show the advantages in ranging improvement. Furthermore, the target ranging method is proposed and the detection performance is analyzed, for the direct-detection manner. Simulation results show the effectiveness of this new ranging scheme. This work is important for enhancing the terahertz radar operation range and can advance the remote sensing applications of terahertz technology.

articleTitle: The Design of Conformal and Chaotic Electromagnetic Stealth Metasurface for Arbitrary NURBS Curved Surfaces
abstract: The conformal design of electromagnetic stealth metasurface that suitable for arbitrary curved surface objects has been lack of study so far. Based on stationary phase method and chaotic distributed scattering, which is a detailed technology of physical optics theory, a new “chaotic projection mapping method” is given to design the metasurface for arbitrary NURBS (Non-uniform rational B-spline) surfaces. Aiming at the difficulties of electromagnetic analysis in the target-oriented design of curved metasurfaces, a new design process with the stealth frequency bands as origin is proposed. The RCS (radar cross section) reduction effect relative to the PEC (ideal electrical conductor) surface of the same shape is analyzed through simulation to verify the effectiveness of this design process.

articleTitle: Study on Electromagnetic Sensitivity of Ku-band Stepped Frequency Radar
abstract: In order to improve the combat capability of radar equipment in the battlefield electromagnetic environment, taking a certain type of stepped frequency radar as the test object, and the continuous wave electromagnetic radiation test is carried out by using all-level irradiation method to reveal the law of continuous wave electromagnetic radiation effect of radar equipment. The results show that the peak level of target echo is suppressed under different interference frequencies. In view of the shortage of research on electromagnetic radiation sensitivity of radar equipment, the electromagnetic sensitivity test is carried out to determine the sensitivity criterion of radar equipment, which lays a good foundation for exploring radar equipment's battlefield survivability.

articleTitle: Design of an electronically steerable dielectric helical antenna phased array for millimeter wave applications
abstract: An electronically steerable dielectric helical antenna phased array for millimeter wave applications is designed in this paper. The phased array consists of three dielectric helical antenna units, a coaxial probe feed port and two grounding ports with tunable capacitor. Its center frequency is 29.7 GHz, effective axial ratio bandwidth is 660 MHz, peek gain is 10.3 dBi, radiation efficiency is over 90%. In addition, the phased array has beam scanning function of ± 20 degrees at the center frequency. The simulation results show that the electronically steerable phased dielectric helical antenna array can be used in millimeter wave wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Design of a Millimeter-wave Bandpass Filter with Computer-aided Tuning Method
abstract: In this paper, a millimeter-wave bandpass filter is designed through a computer-aided tuning (CAT) software which is based on vector fitting (VF) to extract parameters. The actual coupling matrix is generated by extracting equivalent circuit parameters from the simulation file utilizing generalized Chebyshev filter characteristic polynomial synthesis, coupling matrix synthesis. The tuning process is assisted by comparing the extracted coupling matrix and the ideal one. An eighth-order bandpass filter with the center frequency at 35GHz is fabricated for verification. The results show that this software has a clear guiding significance for bandpass filter tuning.

articleTitle: Crosstalk and Equivalent Circuit Model of Segmented Coplanar Waveguide Transmission Line at 5G FR2 Band
abstract: With the improvement of miniaturization and integration of the system, transmission lines need to meet the requirements of high frequency and high speed, eliminate signal crosstalk to the maximum, and improve the signal integrity of the system. In this paper, a flexible segmented coplanar waveguide (SCPW) transmission line structure at 5G FR2 band is proposed, and the crosstalk mechanism of the transmission line is analyzed by using the equivalent circuit model. On this basis, the electromagnetic characteristics of one-unit and three-units, conventional and 100mm interconnects in the 0-45 GHz frequency band are simulated and analyzed. When the crosstalk is −40/−50dB from 20GHz to 45GHz, the distance between conventional one-unit SCPWs is 1.4mm. It is found that the mutual capacitance and mutual inductance between SCPWs is increased with the line length and the number of units. Furthermore, the near end crosstalk and far end crosstalk are seriously affected. This SCPW with appropriate line length and units can be used for 5G millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide
abstract: This paper proposes a new broadband circularly polarized (CP) antenna for 5G millimeter waves based on the integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW). The broadband circularly polarized antenna etches a rectangular slot on the PEC on the upper surface of the ISGW, and then adds two rectangular perturbation patches of different shapes on the rectangular slot, thereby realizing circularly polarized wave radiation. To expand the 10dB return loss bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth of the slot circular polarization antenna based on the substrate integrated gap waveguide, a new dielectric plate is added above the ISGW, and a cross-shaped patch is added above the dielectric plate. This cross-shaped patch not only functions as a parasitic patch but also circularly polarized radiation, thereby achieving the purpose of expanding the 10dB return loss bandwidth and axial ratio bandwidth of the circularly polarized antenna.

articleTitle: A Remote-Reference-Free Parametric Method for Robust Magnetotelluric Impedance Tensor Estimation Evaluated at Several USArray Sites
abstract: We propose a practical and efficient parametric impedance tensor estimation method which determines an Output-Error (OE) based mathematical model based on system identification. In this study, we comprehensively analyze MT impedance tensor estimates to validate the robustness and potential of the parametric method when applied to USArray MT sites with different data quality. The results demonstrate obvious improvement in bias correction of transfer impedance estimates without referencing another site and a best fit accuracy of 91% for validating geo-electric field predictions.

articleTitle: The Inversion of Material Parameters Based on FFT Twofold Subspace-Based Optimization Method
abstract: The inversion of material parameters has gradually become a research hot topic in the field of microwave and terahertz technology. This paper aims to solve the inversion of material parameters, which is the actual application of microwave imaging. The FFT Twofold Subspace-Based Optimization Method (FFT-TSOM), which was proposed by Zhong Yu and Xudong Chen, is a kind of microwave imaging method with good performance. Firstly, this paper summarizes the permittivity selection of scatterers in many literatures, and then FFT-TSOM is used as the inversion algorithm to compare the performance for the imaging of scatterers with larger real and larger imaginary parts. The limitations of the algorithms can be seen. Finally, prospects and directions for future work are discussed.

articleTitle: Design of X-Ku band broadband high-performance and high-integration T / R module
abstract: Based on the urgent need of T/R module engineering in microwave broadband active phased array system, an X-Ku band broadband high-performance and high-integration T/R module with eight channels is proposed in this paper, aiming at solving the problems of traditional T/R module, such as insufficient bandwidth, large size, poor stability and low precision of phase shift and attenuation. The T/R module is realized basing on the breakthrough of eight channels module architecture design technique, high-density integrated design technique based on LTCC entire board, high reliability and high efficiency and heat dissipation design technique of broadband GaN power amplifier, high-frequency broadband high isolation cavity effect design technique, modularization design and mass manufacturability design technique. The main functions of transceiver amplification, amplitude and phase control and safety protection are obtained in this module. The measured results show that the output power in the whole frequency band is ≥ 23.9W, the noise figure is ≤ 3.52dB, the phase shifting accuracy is ≤ 4.87° (RMS), the attenuation accuracy is ≤ 0.87dB (RMS), the standing wave ratio is ≤ 2.0, and the efficiency is ≥23%. Among them, the working bandwidth index increases from 10-12GHz and 15-17GHz to 10-18GHz, the output power increases from 10W to 20W, and the noise figure decreases from 4.3dB to less than 4.0dB. This module has the characteristics of high frequency, wide band, high efficiency and high integration. It can be used in new integrated sensor radar system, multifunctional integrated electronic system, etc.

articleTitle: Terahertz Metasurface Design with Arbitrary Hexagon Patterns Based on Deep Learning
abstract: For the metasurface design, a novel unit cell of arbitrary hexagon patterns and a neural network that can generate these patterns are proposed to get target transmission amplitudes and phases at will. The hexagon patterns are encoded to few design variables but retain high design freedom and fabrication feasibility. Long short-term memory is applied to the neural network to provide meaningful design parameters. A terahertz transmissive metasurface lens that consists of the generated patterns is simulated to further verify the design concept. This work provides a new solution to the inverse design of metasurface and opportunities for the future of multi-functional terahertz devices.

articleTitle: Study on Continuous Wave Electromagnetic Interference Effect of UAV Data Link
abstract: Data link “front door” coupling is the main reason that leads to the electromagnetic interference of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). In order to master the experimental rule of data link in the continuous-wave (CW) electromagnetic environment, this paper takes the L-band data link as the experimental object, analyzes the “field-path” conversion of interference signal theoretically, and conducts the electromagnetic sensitivity (EMS) test by using injection method. The experimental results show that under different working signal intensities, the changing rules of the losing-lock threshold of data link are basically the same, and the data link has sensitive frequency bands in and out of the communication band, among which the main reason for the out-of-band (OOB) interference is the generation of second harmonic interference in the intermediate frequency (IF) processing section.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Line used for Probe Calibration up to 40 GHz
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G communication, the electromagnetic interference (EMI) becomes more serious than before. For the EMI diagnosis, there is a great demand for the magnetic probe working at millimeter-waves. The design of two low-cost kinds of microstrip lines used for probe calibration up to 40 GHz are proposed in this paper. Their features, including S parameter and working field components, are both presented in detail. Both numerical and physical results verify the effectiveness of these two structures which can be used to calculate the correct probe factor at a high frequency.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Filtering Magic-T Based on Microstrip Transmission Line
abstract: In this paper, a new filtering magic-T based on microstrip transmission lines is presented. By utilizing two dual-mode resonators and 1/2 λ transmission line, the configuration of a magic-T can be obtained, which can operate with desired filtering response, port-to-port phase property as well as good isolation. To validate the proposed concept and method, a prototype filtering magic-T working at 1.9GHz has been implemented. The simulation results indicate that the filtering magic-T exhibits nice operation performance.

articleTitle: High–Gain Folded Reflectarray Antenna Operating at 1 THz
abstract: Compact, high-gain and high-efficiency antennas are in high demand for future 6G terabit-per-bit wireless communications systems. This paper introduces a novel silicon-based folded reflectarray antenna operating at 1 THz as a high-gain THz antenna solution. The antenna consists of an open-ended waveguide, bottom main reflectarray layer and an upper polarizer. The anisotropic dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is employed as the building block of the bottom main reflectarray to realize simultaneous phase compensation and polarization conversion. The THz folded reflectarray antenna was fabricated using photolithography and deep reactive ion etching of high-resistivity silicon wafers. Both simulated and measured results verified that the proposed THz folded reflectarray antenna can realize high directivity at 1 THz.

articleTitle: A Midfield Wireless Energy Transmission Antenna Based on Metamaterial for Implanted Capsule Endoscope
abstract: Aiming at the wireless power transmission (WPT) problem of capsule endoscope, a 1.4GHz wireless power transmission antenna is proposed. Because of the negative permittivity and permeability of metamaterials, a split resonant ring (SRR) structure is designed to enhance the characteristics of energy convergence antenna and improve the efficiency of energy transmission. The antenna size is 28.5mm ×13mm×0.085mm. The performance of the antenna in three-layer structure simulation is analyzed. Experiment results proved that the antenna has good transmission effect under the safety standard. By comparing the simulation results with the measured results, the good consistency between them is verified.

articleTitle: Phaseless Terahertz Coded-Aperture Imaging Based on Generative Model
abstract: Phaseless terahertz coded-aperture imaging (PL-TCAI) is a promising radar imaging technology that leverage the coded aperture antenna and phase recovery algorithm to achieve high-resolution, forward-looking and staring imaging without relying on relative motion. As is known, it is a severely ill-conditioned inverse problem to solve the target scattering coefficient only from intensity measurements. To relieve the illnesses and reduce the demand for intensity measurements for target reconstruction, a PL-TCAI method based on generative model is proposed. This method utilizes the alternate minimization algorithm to find the ground truth under the prior information provided by the generative model. Simulation experiments show that the proposed method can reconstruct target under low intensity measurements, and it has a competitive performance with the state-of-the-art algorithm.

articleTitle: Cascaded Split-Ring Resonator for Decoupling of Broadband Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna Array
abstract: A cascaded split-ring resonator (SRR) is introduced to reduce the mutual coupling of antenna elements in broadband dual-polarized base station array, which is printed on one side of a 1mm thickness FR4 substrate. By using of this type of cascaded SRR, the band gap used to reduce the mutual coupling of elements can be broaden remarkably, it then be used in dual-polarized base station antenna array. The simulated results show that this structure can improve the isolation between dual-polarized base station antennas over the band of 1.71GHz-2.69GHz (44.5% relative bandwidth), and narrow the half-power beam width (HPBW) of the array simultaneously, which can be used for the decoupling of 4G and 5G broadband dual polarization base station array in the future.

articleTitle: Double-Layer Broadband and Wide Beam Microstrip Array Antenna For 79GHz Automotive Radar
abstract: A double-layer broadband and wide beam microstrip antenna is presented for 79GHz automotive radar. The antenna is composed of a microstrip line, a radiation patch and a parasitic patch. In addition, the radiation patch is fed by the microstrip line in the form of coupling feed. The parasitic patch on the top substrate is designed for wider band. Based on the double-layer elements, a 10-elements standing-wave linear array is constructed, which have broadband with 5 GHz from 76GHz to 81GHz. Besides, the array antenna can achieve a wide beam of 115° in the azimuth plane and a low side-lobe less than -20dB in the elevation plane.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave MIMO imaging radar with an ultra-high angular resolution of 0.6 degree
abstract: A new cascading multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar at V-band with 192 virtual elements is developed. The experiment for imaging indoor and outfield is performed with an angular resolution of 0.6°. In addition, sparse array with 108 virtual elements based on this platform is tested with genetic algorithm, the imaging results show that the sparse array imaging with a sparse rate of 55.1% agree well with full array.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Metasurface Antenna Based on Substrate Integrated Double Line
abstract: A dual-slot fed circularly polarized metasurface (MTS) antenna based on the substrate integrated double line (SIDL) technology is presented in this paper. The proposed consists of a MTS which is made up of an array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> periodic metal patches, a SIDL and the dual-slot which coupled the energy to the MTS. The simulated results show a −10-dB impedance bandwidth is from 24.03 GHz to 26.45 GHz, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is from 24.36 GHz to 26.44 GHz and the peak gain is 8.98 dBi at 25.4GHz.

articleTitle: Multilayer Slot Coupling Ultra-wideband Power Divider Based on Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide
abstract: In this paper, based on the integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW), an ultra-wideband power divider using multilayer slot coupling technology is designed for 5G and satellite radar applications. The power divider used the ISGW which is composed of a via layer and a gap layer and transmitted energy from a coupling patch on transmission ridge of bottom layer through coupling slot to coupling patch on transmission ridge of top layer. This design has good isolation after adding the isolation resistor to a modified position. The simulated results show that return loss of the power divider is less than 10-dB, which the bandwidth can reach at least 15.7 GHz from 20.2GHz to 35.9 GHz. Also, the best insertion loss in a band is 3.53dB. The isolation degree is always better than 15-dB in 22.2GHz-35.4GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of the Dual-Band Negative Group Delay Circuit Based on Taguchi Method
abstract: In this paper, A defected microstrip structure (DMS) design is presented for dual-band negative group delay circuit (NGDC). The frequency and group delay of each band are influenced by DMS. To promise the match of the goal frequencies, Taguchi Method (TM) is chosen to optimize the NGDC. To validate the design concept, a prototype of this NGDC has been designed, optimized, simulated and fabricated. Its electromagnetic and circuit-simulated results agree well. From the measurements, at 3.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz, the negative group delay (NGD) values are achieved -3.5 ns and -6.5 ns respectively.

articleTitle: A 128-GHz Broadband CMOS Amplifier with Distributed Resonance Frequencies of Parasitic Shunt LC Resonators
abstract: The realization of ultra-high-speed wireless communications in the 300-GHz band is expected. A 300-GHz transceiver requires broadband intermediate-frequency amplifiers in the D-band. To realize a broadband amplifier in the D-band, we propose an amplifier with distributed resonance frequencies of shunt LC resonators. The resonators are composed of the gate-to-drain parasitic capacitances and the shunt inductors in the gate-side intermediate networks. To achieve a flat frequency response, the number of high frequency resonators should be greater than the number of low frequency resonators. The proposed amplifier is fabricated using a 45-nm SOI CMOS process. It is shown that the proposed amplifier has the center frequency of 128 GHz, the gain of 10.4 dB and the −3 dB bandwidth of 19 GHz. The performance of the proposed amplifier is compared to the state-of-the-art CMOS amplifiers, and it is shown that the proposed amplifier achieves wide bandwidth in the D-band.

articleTitle: Wide Angle Scanning Leaky Wave Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna for Satellite Communications
abstract: In this paper, a leaky-wave antenna for 5G/6G/VSAT applications based on the substrate integrated waveguide structure (SIW) for X/K frequency band operation has been presented. The proposed antenna has periodic rectangular and H-shaped slots on the radiating layer. The frequency sweep from 10.1-12.5GHz (and 18-22GHz for K version) lead to antenna beam scanning from broadside to end-fire (2 to 90 degrees). The structures can be utilized in satellite/radar communications/direction finding systems, provide beam scanning patterns with frequency sweep and are capable of preventing communication interferences between satellites.

Author Keywords: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Leaky Wave Antenna (SIWLWA)

articleTitle: A Self-Packaged Wide Stopband Bandpass Filter Using Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide
abstract: This paper proposes a wide stopband filter based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW) technology. The ISGW wide stopband filter structure is composed of three-layer dielectric substrates. The top substrate uses metallic via-holes and metallic patches to achieve a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) structure. It is suitable for package substrates and integrated waveguide (SIW) filters. The middle layer substrate provides a stable gap layer, and the base substrate is used to obtain the SIW filter by etching the dumbbell slot in the mental plane, i.e. the self-packaged ISGW filter. The center frequency of the filter is 10.9GHz, and the simulation results show that the return loss in the passband is better than 25dB, and the out-of-band rejection in the 12.2 GHz - 19 GHz frequency band is better than 40dB, achieving a wider stopband.

articleTitle: A Method for Extracting DEM From CSAR Sub-aperture Correlation
abstract: Because of CSAR can obtain the characteristics of the total scattering information of the target area. This paper proposes a method that only needs single-circle echo data to survey the terrain of the observation scene and get the DEM. The echo data is divided into several arcs, and the arcs' correlation is used to obtain the terrain undulations of the observation area. This paper proposed a method to get the observation scenes' terrain undulations using the geometric deformation and correlation between the sub-aperture images. The proposed method is validated by the CSAR data at Ku band.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Terahertz High-order Mode Power Coupler for Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Amplifiers
abstract: The design and simulation of a terahertz high-order mode power coupler for sheet beam traveling wave amplifiers are presented in this paper. The proposed power coupler has functions of both the mode conversion and the beam wave convergence/separation. To improve the performance of this structure, some auxiliary structures are introduced, including a rectangular septum, a matching step and a pair of symmetric Bragg reflectors. The proposed power coupler has numerous competitive advantages, such as broad bandwidth, high transmission coefficient and high conversion efficiency, high port isolation, low port reflection, and high mode purity.

articleTitle: Conformal Antenna of Cylindrical Carrier Based on Jet Printing Technology
abstract: A nonplanar antenna of cylindrical carrier based on jet printing technology is proposed in this letter. The antenna uses jet printing technology to print the circular radiation patch on the outer surface of the cylindrical dielectric carrier, and the feed network is attached to the inner surface of the cylindrical dielectric carrier by plane bending. The shape of the antenna is conformal to the surface of a cylinder such that the antenna can be completely integrated within the body of a cylindrical carrier without protruding components. Therefore, the antenna design concept would enable the integration of antenna arrays on small aeronautical platforms. We have studied and analyzed the difference in the characteristics between planar antenna element and conformal antenna element. The simulation results show that the operating frequency band is from 2.5 to 3.2 GHz, so the antenna can be used for satellite communication of aircraft platform.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Liquid Permittivity Measurement with Effective Localized Surface Plasmons
abstract: In this talk, I will give a scheme to measure the liquid complex permittivity with high sensitivity based an ultra compact effective localized surface plasmons (ELSPs) sensor. Sharp resonance induced by the ELSPs resonator greatly enhance the sensitivity of the measurement. To estimate the complex permittivity of arbitrary unknown liquid, we establish an equivalent circuit model of this ELSPs sensor and build a fitting model based on the frequency shift and return loss. For demonstration, we successfully p redict the complex permittivity of ethanol from 0 to 90% with high precision. This ELSPs based sensor with an ultra compact size of 0.008 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}^{2}$</tex> and high sensitivity of 0.57% can find many applications (liquid permi ttivity measurement, liquid concentration, liquid testing, etc.) in highly integrated systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient Detection Method for Maneuvering Target with Multiple Motion Models
abstract: This paper addresses the detection problem for a maneuvering target with multiple motion models. That is, during the integration time, the motion model of the target is not single. In this paper, the motion model change point is firstly determined. Then, the motion model judgment and parameters estimation for different motion stages are completed. Finally, well-focused image of the target is obtained after motion compensation. The numerical experiment verifies the performance of the method in target detection.

articleTitle: X-Band Ridged Waveguide Power Combiner
abstract: A X-band ridged waveguide power combiner is proposed and designed by adopting the ridge waveguide-microstrip probe transition structure. A low insertion loss is achieved from the fabricated ridge waveguide structure. It provides a solution for the future research in miniaturized power combination application.

articleTitle: Dual polarized Antenna and Array with Filtering Response and Low Cross Polarization for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
abstract: A millimeter wave (mmWave) dual polarized antenna with filtering response and low cross polarization for the fifth generation (5G) mobile communications is proposed. The isolation better than 20 dB between two feeding ports was achieved with the two ports in the same plane. The antenna is low profile with only 1.4 mm thickness including two dielectric layers and a bounding layer. The operating frequency band is from 26.5 GHz to 29.5 GHz, which can be applied to n257 5G mmWave band. In addition, a rotating sequence 2 ×2 antenna array is designed and measured. The same polarization is fed by a differential feeding network, which will further reduce the cross polarization of the array, the cross polarization is better than 20 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Sparse MIMO Array Imaging System Based on Millimeter-wave Band
abstract: In this paper, a novel millimeter-wave sparse multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array imaging system with a working frequency of 70-80GHz is presented. In this system, 8 identical millimeter-wave radio frequency (RF) front-end modules are integrated and a self-designed sparse linear array structure is adopted, in which 93% of the transmitting channels and 50% of the receiving channels are reduced while ensuring the imaging quality. The sparse linear array can not only reduce the required cost, but also shorten the data acquisition time. In addition, to make the equivalent phase center (EPC) array evenly distributed and almost no redundancy, a new array working method is proposed, which can achieve fast image reconstruction of the target after combining with the range migration algorithm (RMA). Experimental results prove the high-resolution imaging capability of the designed millimeter-wave sparse MIMO array imaging system.

articleTitle: Simulation of Transmission Pipeline Defects based on Microwave
abstract: A novel method to detect the defect location and corrosion degree of petroleum pipelines by microwave is proposed in this paper. Three hypotheses are set in the simulation experiment: (a) intact oil pipeline; (b) corrosive oil pipeline; (c) broken oil pipeline. Among them, the flawed oil pipelines are divided into different grades according to different defect depths in the experiment. The probe is scanned on the pipe, and then the waveform of the scattering parameter (S11) is simulated. When the curve fluctuates, it means that the pipeline at the fluctuating place is incomplete, and can classify defects according to the amplitude of fluctuations (degree of corrosion). From the experimental results, we can discover that microwave technology can be used to accurately locate and classify the defects of an oil pipeline.

articleTitle: Compact Multibeam Metasurface Lens Antenna with Circular Polarization for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
abstract: In this article, we introduce a compact multibeam metasurface lens (MSL) antenna with circular polarization for 5G millimeter-wave applications. The constituent meta-atom composed of two coupled slotted patch resonators can achieve a continuous phase shift covering 360° range by rotating the upper patch for circular polarizations. Utilizing three microstrip patch antennas as the feeding sources, the MSL antenna can provide radiating beam along vertical or ± 30° from vertical direction. The proposed MSL antenna has an aperture size of 3.36 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×3.36 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and a focal-to-diameter ratio of 0.11. The maximum gain for vertical or ± 30° from vertical beam is 13.8, or 12.3 dBi around 27 GHz, respectively. The proposed design features the advantages of compact size, easy integration, low cost and light weight, which may be further used for multibeam or beam scanning applications in modern wireless communication.

articleTitle: A NUFFT-Based Frequency-Domain Imaging Algorithm for Single-Input Non-Uniform Multiple-Output Array
abstract: As a more general Single-Input Multiple-Output array, Single-Output Non-Uniform Multiple-Input arrays are rarely studied. In this regard, this paper proposes a frequency domain imaging algorithm based on Non-Uniform Fourier transform, which uses non-uniform Fourier transform technology to transform the spatial signal received by radar to frequency domain for three-dimensional imaging processing. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can obtain imaging resolution and Peak Side Lobe Ratio similar to the BP algorithm, but the imaging time is much shorter than that of the BP algorithm.

articleTitle: An Accurate Semi-Numerical Approach for Bi-Layer Metasurfaces with Inter-Layer Coupling
abstract: In this communication, we present an accurate equivalent circuit model based on the transmission-line theory and Floquet theory for bi-layer metasurfaces, studying the inter-layer coupling caused by the high-order harmonics.

articleTitle: A High Gain Circularly Polarized Microstrip Array Antenna At Millimeter-Wave Band
abstract: This paper presents the design of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{4} \times \mathrm{4}$</tex> elements circularly polarized microstrip patch array at millimeter-wave band. The sequential rotation method and series-parallel feed network are employed in the power distribution circuit for antenna performance improvement. The feed network is integrated on the same substrate layer of the antenna array in order to facilitate processing and manufacturing, and the total size of the design is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{10} \text{mm}\times \mathrm{12} \text{mm}\times \mathrm{0.127} \text{mm}$</tex>. The simulated return loss exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 7%, and the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 10% with respect to 78.5 GHz is obtained. Besides, the maximal gain is 17.6dBi at 78.5GHz.

articleTitle: Advances in Artificial Neural Networks for Electromagnetic Parameterized Modeling
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) parameterized modeling is important for EM repetitive analysis, such as EM optimization, what if analysis, and yield optimization. An overview of advances in artificial neural networks (ANNs) for EM parameterized modeling is presented in this paper, covering forward/inverse modeling, deep neural networks, knowledge-based neural networks, neuro-transfer functions, and applications for fast EM modeling with varying values in geometrical parameters.

articleTitle: Flexible Microwave Plasmonic Sensor for Noninvasive Measurement of Blood Glucose
abstract: In this paper, a flexible microwave plasmonic sensor for noninvasive measurement of blood glucose has been demonstrated. Using inkjet printing technology, metal corrugated ring is printed on the flexible surface to form a localized surface plasmons resonator. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) microfluidic channel is used to simulate the complex blood vessels of human body, which are placed under the resonator. The experimental and simulation results show that the flexible sensor has the advantages of high sensitivity and good robustness. The sensor has great potential in monitoring blood glucose.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna with Simple Feeding
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) unidirectional antenna is proposed in this paper. By employing a slot antenna and a pair of horizontal plates as a magnetic dipole and an electric dipole, respectively, the proposed magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna is designed for CP radiation. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1-\lambda$</tex> resonant mode of the proposed ME dipole antenna is excited by a single feeding to achieve a wideband characteristic. Simulated results show that the antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth (IMBW) of 4.77-5.5 GHz (0.73 GHz, 14.2%) and 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 4.3-5.5 GHz (1.2 GHz, 24.5%). In addition, unidirectional radiation patterns with a peak gain of 5.6 dBi and high radiation efficiency of more than 90% over the operating band are obtained.

articleTitle: An SICL-Fed Open Loop Antenna with an Enhanced Bandwidth for 5G Millimeter-Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, a planar loop antenna based on substrate-integrated coaxial line (SICL) feed is proposed for the 5G millimeter-wave communications. This fundamental antenna consists of an open-loop pair. The position of the arc-shaped cut in the loop is used to adjust the surface current to enhance the bandwidth. Compared with the traditional monopole antennas, the proposed scheme has a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{15.7}\times \mathrm{9.8}\times \mathrm{0.678}\ \text{mm}^{\mathrm{3}}$</tex>. An impedance bandwidth (from 21.8 GHz to 49.8 GHz) with a peak gain of 7 dBi at 37.0 GHz is confirmed in the simulation, whereafter an additional loop pair of the same dimensions are attached along the longitudinal direction to the original one and realizes a peak gain of 8.1 dBi.

articleTitle: The Compact Filtering Dielectric Antenna Based on Dielectric Strip Resonator
abstract: A compact filtering dielectric antenna (FDA) based on dielectric strip resonator (DSR) is proposed to achieve filtering response without gain reduction. A compact size is achieved by using a ceramic material with a high dielectric constant operated in the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">δ1</sub> cavity mode is analyzed. By utilizing the parallel placed microstrip line to fed the DSR, the filtering response is obtained with no gain reduction. In comparison with the reported design, the proposed one has the advantages of compact size, no gain reduction and wide stopband. To demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed antenna, one prototype is fabricated that operates at 4.9 GHz, achieved good performance characteristics and verified the rationality of the principle.

articleTitle: Engineeringly Equivalent Method of Replacing High Field Radiation for Two-wire System
abstract: To simplify the operation steps of bulk current injection (BCI) instead of high field radiation test and ensure the error is within the controllable range, the analysis and calculation model of the response of the equipment under test (EUT) has been established without a current probe under radiation condition and a current probe under injection condition. The engineeringly equivalent method of bulk current injection replacing high field intensity radiation test is proposed and verified by test. The research results show that the equivalent test error can be controlled within 1dB, which meets the actual requirements of the project.

articleTitle: Antenna Directivity Estimation of Millimeter-Wave Mobile Terminals Using Single Radio Sensor
abstract: High spatial frequency utilization efficiency is expected in the millimeter-wave band. In this paper, we propose an antenna direction estimation method of mobile terminals (MTs) by the envelope fluctuation of the reception power. The antenna directivity estimation accuracy of the proposed method is evaluated by computer simulation. The result shows that it was confirmed that the antenna directivity estimation accuracy was more than ±90% for the angle against the movement direction, and was more than ±50% for the angle perpendicular to the movement direction even when receiving the radio wave radiated from the side lobe of the directional antenna.

articleTitle: Inverse Design for WB-BGA Package Structure by Deep Learning
abstract: During the package design process, a lot of simulation even measurement need to be carried out to ensure the package can fulfill regulatory radiation standards. In general, full-wave simulation is time-consuming when adjusting the structural parameters of the package to obtain the far-field radiation. In this paper, an inverse design method based on a convolution neural network is proposed to quickly optimize and design the package structure. The cascade model combining an inverse design network and a forward predicted network can help the convergence of the inverse network. The feasibility and effectiveness of the inverse design method are finally demonstrated through a set of true radiation data.

articleTitle: Compact and Broadband Multi-aperture Coupler for Terahertz Sheet Beam Travelling Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper, a compact and broadband directional multi-aperture waveguide coupler was initially designed for terahertz sheet beam travelling wave tubes. The proposed coupler is based on a series of identical apertures distributed between a pair of parallel rectangular waveguides. Simulation results predicted that the bandwidth for the coupling coefficient greater than -1 dB was 81.3 GHz (220.0-301.3 GHz), corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 31.2%. Meanwhile, the reflection of all ports was lower than -15 dB, and the maximum isolation coefficient was below -15 dB.

articleTitle: A Liquid Crystal Frequency Tunable Antenna with Larger Tuning Range
abstract: A liquid crystal frequency tunable antenna with larger tuning range is presented. It is a traditional patch antenna, which is divided into four parts by three slots. Benefiting from the slots, this antenna can operate in TM10 mode and antiphase TM20 mode within the same frequency band. Through choosing the tunable material liquid crystal as the dielectric of the antenna, the resonant frequency of the two modes can be tuned at the same time. Consequently, the frequency tuning range of this antenna is doubled as compared with the traditional liquid crystal microstrip patch antenna. The simulation results show that the resonant frequency tuning range of the proposed antenna is from 21.7 GHz to 23.9 GHz (9.6%), which is two times bigger than that of traditional liquid crystal microstrip patch antenna (4.8%).

articleTitle: Switchable circular dichroism resonators for spin selective absorption
abstract: The circular dichroism resonator (CDR) can produce spin selective absorption for left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) waves. However, in the microwave band, the previously proposed CDRs only absorb designated CP waves and lack versatility in practical applications. Here, we propose a switchable CDR based on a pair of PIN diodes. It switches between the left-hand and right-hand CDR modes through the alternate ON-OFF of two PIN diodes. The left-hand CDR absorbs LCP waves and converts RCP waves into LCP waves. The opposite is true for the right-hand CDR. The thickness of the switchable CDR is one-tenth of the working wavelength, which is suitable for integrated manufacturing.

articleTitle: Optimization design of negative group delay circuits based on improved PSO algorithm
abstract: Based on electromagnetic simulation and catfish particle swarm algorithm, a novel method is proposed to design the negative group delay circuit with defected structures. The optimization is developed to increase the efficiency and the accuracy, which is confirmed by the data before and after optimizations. The measured results show that at the frequencies of 5.7 and 7.0 GHz, the insertion loss values achieve -17dB and -7dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Polygonal RFID Tag Antenna
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of miniaturization of RFID tag antenna, this paper proposes a design scheme of polygonal ring dipole tag antenna based on the bent arm structure. Parameter analysis is carried out to study the influence of polygon structure on antenna size and input impedance. The antenna has characteristics of simple fabrication, small size and low sensitivity to environment, and has potential application value in RFID systems.

articleTitle: Influence of Diffuse Reflection on Field Uniformity in Electromagnetic Interference Testing Chamber
abstract: The evaluation method of reverberation chamber performance, the function and working principle of mechanical stirrer are described. The effect of diffuse reflection on the uniformity of field intensity in mechanical stirring reverberation chamber was analyzed by electromagnetic simulation software. The simulation results show that the introduction of diffuse reflector can improve the field uniformity of reverberation chamber, and the effect depends on the design and number of diffuse reflector surfaces.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Millimeter Wave Propagation in Underdense Homogeneous Plasma
abstract: In this paper, the simulation model of millimeter wave reflected, absorbed and transmitted characteristics in underdense uniform plasma is established. The calculation of reflection energy, transmission energy and absorption energy of millimeter wave is completed. The frequency of millimeter wave is 50-100GHz, and other parameters such as polarization, incident angle, plasma length are different. The results are shown that the propagation characteristics of millimeter wave in plasma are the same although polarization is different. Thin plasma can hardly absorb millimeter wave energy; when the plasma has centimeter scale, the millimeter wave energy can be absorbed more than 95% by optimizing the plasma parameters. The propagation characteristics of millimeter wave at different incident angles are obviously different.

articleTitle: Expansion Technique of the Beamforming Area for 60-GHz-Band Beamforming Array Antenna in Mobile Wireless Terminal Application
abstract: This invited paper reviews an expansion technique of the beamforming area for 60-GHz-band beamforming array antenna in mobile wireless terminal application. Two expansion technique for phi and theta angles are reviewed. Two dipole subarrays are utilized for phi angle expansion. On the other hand, dipole and patch subarrays are employed for theta angle expansion. The proposed technique is verified by 3-D electromagnetic field simulation and measurement. We confirmed the beamforming area was successfully expanded for desired angle by the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Sparse Array Antenna Based on LPDA
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband wide-angle scanning sparse array antenna is proposed in this paper. The log periodic dipole antenna with exponential shape is selected as the unit of sparse array antenna due to its small size, ultra-wideband and non-frequency-dependent characteristics. After the unit design is completed, genetic algorithm is used to optimize the array layout efficiently, and the final number of units is determined to be 40. The aperture area of the sparse array is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{300}\_\text{mm} \times \mathrm{300}\_\text{mm}$</tex>. Compared to the conventional periodic array, the proposed sparse array has reduced about 190 antenna units. Through optimization of performance and position of the element, the sparse array can achieve active <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{VSWR} < \mathrm{3}$</tex> and S11 < −10dB in the ultra-wideband of 3 – 12GHz (120%). Simulation results show that the beam pointing accuracy is better than 10 degrees, the azimuth scanning angle is plus or minus 45 degrees, and the pitching scanning angle is plus or minus 30 degrees. The gain at the center frequency 7GHz is about 22dBi.

articleTitle: Numerical Studies of Light Brightness Emitted by Microwave Nitrogen Breakdown in Circular Waveguide
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional (3D) multiphysics model coupling full-wave Maxwell's equations with plasma fluid equations is used to analyze the light characteristics during high-power microwave (HPW) nitrogen breakdown in circular waveguide. In this process, balance equations of an excited molecule (ion) density are introduced into the fluid model to describe the light brightness. The resulting multi-physics system is analyzed with the spectral-element time-domain (SETD) method. The electron density and light brightness in the high electric field initially increases sharply over time. After the occurrence of the breakdown, electron density and light brightness saturate at a high level. The position of the maximum light brightness spot moves toward the microwave source. Our research provides theoretical guidance for Comprehensively exploring and understanding physical phenomena in microwave nitrogen breakdown.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Circuital-Thermal Multiphysics Simulation Based on DGTD and FETD Method with Higher-Order Basis Functions
abstract: With the continuous improvement of the technological level of integrated circuits (ICs), the operating frequency and integration density are becoming higher and higher, which brings huge challenges to the simulation of integrated circuits. On one hand, the wave effect becomes noticeable as the working frequency increases. For instance, the electromagnetic coupling between the interconnects and package will lead to the signal integrity problem. In this situation, the simulation accuracy cannot be guaranteed if only the classical circuit theory is adopted. Therefore, full-wave electromagnetic simulation method must be included to implement electromagnetic-circuital cosimulation. On the other hand, high integration level will not only raise the density of the devices and interconnects, but also increase the power density, resulting in difficulties in thermal management. As a result, the mutual effects between EM and thermal must also be taken into account. To sum up, the electromagnetic-circuital-thermal multiphysics simulation becomes necessary and significant in the design of ICs. In this paper, an electromagnetic-thermal co-simulation method based on discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method and finite-element time-domain (FETD) method with higher order basis functions is proposed. The DGTD method is utilized for EM simulation [2], while the FETD method is adopted for thermal simulation [3]–[5]. The higher order hierachical basis function is utilized to decrease the mesh density and reduce the number of spatial unknowns. The large-scale parallel computing technique based on message passing interface (MPI) is employed to accelerate both the DGTD and FETD algorithm. Numerical examples are computed on distributed clusters to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Development of a G-band Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube with Peak Power 60W Bandwidth 6GHz
abstract: In present work, we report a terahertz (THz) travelling wave tube (TWT) with two cascade sections, which has high power and broad-bandwidth. The operation voltage and operation current of electron beam are 17.18 kV and 71 mA, respectively. Using such electron beam, the peak power of TWT is 60 W at the frequency of 0.22THz. Besides, the gain is over 30 dB at over 6 GHz bandwidth. Such new THz TWT will be applicated in long-range radar and high-speed communication systems.

articleTitle: Advances of Equivalent Modeling Theory and Method in the Analysis and Design of Electromagnetic Metamaterials
abstract: Electromagnetic metamaterials (EMM) are a new kind of artificial synthetic material, and they have attracted extensive attention from academia and industry because of their special electromagnetic properties that natural substances do not possess. This paper reviews recent advances of equivalent modeling theory and method in the analysis and design of electromagnetic metamaterials. First, equivalent parameters extraction methods of electromagnetic metamaterials based on effective medium theory is briefly summarized. Second, material parameter synthesis using equivalence principle is introduced. Finally, the design method of electromagnetic metamaterials based on wave spectrum expansion theory is proposed.

articleTitle: A Novel Cavity-Backed Slot Array Antenna With Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a novel broadband cavity-backed antenna based on substrate-integrated coaxial line (SICL) technology. The proposed antenna uses the SICL to feed a substrate-integrated backed-cavity and then uses the Chebyshev centimeter network to suppress its sidelobe levels. An electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure is utilized as well to reduce the coupling between the radiating elements. Finally, a relative bandwidth of 10% (5%) of less than -10dB (-15dB) is realized, with a peak gain of 19.2 dBi observed at 40.5GHz. The average value of SLLs in the bandwidth is-16.1 dB (E plane) and -27.2 dB (H plane), and the radiation efficiency of the antenna in the effective bandwidth is greater than 88%.

articleTitle: Humidity sensor based on near zero index media
abstract: Near-zero index (NZI) media has the characteristics of local field enhancement, local tunneling and tunneling effect. Here a humidity sensor based on near-zero permittivity (ENZ) media is proposed, which uses the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The tunnel height of the designed sensor is much smaller than the height of the SIW structure. It can be observed that there exist strong electric fields in the ENZ tunnel. Placing humidity-sensitive materials in the structure can realize a high-sensitivity humidity sensor. When the humidity changes, it is observed that the frequency of the sensor has changed, and its sensitivity is 1.07 MHz/RH, which proves that the sensor can effectively measure the changes in environmental humidity.

articleTitle: Research on The Terahertz Fiber with Negative Curvature
abstract: In this paper, three terahertz fibers based on negative curvature claddings are designed, in which the negative curvature terahertz fiber with nested triangular claddings has a minimum confinement loss of 0.005 dB/cm at 2.36 THz, and the double negative curvature terahertz fiber has a low confinement loss of 4.7 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>dB/cm at 1.28 THz. The multimode orbital angular momentum (OAM) terahertz fiber based on double-layer elliptical cladding structure can reach the confinement loss of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> dB/cm in the frequency range of 0.525 - 0.8 THz, which is beneficial to promote the application of mode division multiplexing (MDM) technology in communication systems.

articleTitle: Particle-In-Cell Simulation of 0.108THz Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: Folded Waveguide (FW) Traveling Wave Tubes (TWT) is a kind of high frequency, high power, and moderate bandwidth slow-wave structures. In many applications, FWTWT is a seductive choice. Such as radars, communication systems and electron counter measure. In this paper, a two-section folded waveguide at 0.108THz is designed to get 50W of average power. The structural parameters and dispersion characteristics of this folded waveguide are optimized through a detailed analysis. Influence of simulation parameters, angle dispersion, energy dispersion and roughness on output power are investigated using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. Analysis the phase velocity on the output power, and the results indicate that the output power can be increased by reducing the phase velocity. The simulation results shows that the maximum output power and gain are about 50W and 30dB at 0.108THz, and the bandwidth of this folded waveguide is about 10GHz, which is driven by an electron beam with operation voltage 13.2KV and current 0.08A.

articleTitle: Design of Transition Circuits for Chip Assembly at Terahertz Band
abstract: In this paper, two transition circuits to assemble chips using coplanar waveguide (CPW) without back conductor at terahertz (THz) band are presented. The first transition circuit is adopting a CPW to microstrip line (MSL) transition circuit. Quarter wavelength radial MSL is used for RF ground connection between CPW and MSL. The second transition circuit is using flip-circuit structure. This transition circuit has CPW pad on one end, and a E-plane probe for CPW to waveguide mode transition. The circuit is suspended in a channel, and flip mounted on the CPW pad of the chip. Impedance matching with several step impedance CPW lines are adopted. All the transition circuits are simulated with HFSS. The results show that the return loss of the radial MSL transition circuit is less than −10dB at 100 to 170 GHz. The return loss of the flip-circuit is less than −15dB at 100 to 170 GHz. Compared with traditional gold wire bonding, the proposed transition structures significantly improve the performance at THz band.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of a Terahertz-band Sheet Beam Extended Interaction Oscillator
abstract: The preliminary design and analysis of a 0.3 THz extended interaction oscillator (EIO) driven by a sheet electron beam is presented in this paper. Its interaction circuit consists of a sheet electron beam tunnel with 17 gaps, two coupling cavities, a coupling waveguide, and a standard rectangular output waveguide. It was optimized to achieve good electrical performance by using the CST-Microwave Studio. The operating mode is the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>-like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{2}\pi$</tex> mode and its corresponding resonant frequency is ∼294.32 GHz. Initial particle-in-cell simulations having considered the ohmic loss demonstrated that the designed EIO could provide a radiation power of 376 W at 294 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-View HRRP Recognition Based on Denoising Features Enhancement
abstract: High resolution range profiles (HRRPs) have always been an important hot spot in radar automatic target recognition (RATR). However, the problem regarding enhancement in data reliability of HRRPs to improve the final recognition accuracy remains challenging. Recent developments in denoising features enhancement and multi-view data processing provide a potential solution to the problem. In this paper, a multi-view HRRP recognition method based on denoising features enhancement is proposed. A denoising network is first proposed to suppress clutter and enhance the ability of features extraction. Then, multi-view data processing is applied to improve the recognition accuracy rate and data reliability. The effectiveness in terms of signal denoising and the improvement in terms of the recognition accuracy rate are validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Multi-physics DGTD Solution for Field-Circuit Co-Simulation
abstract: In this paper, an innovative multi-physics DGTD solution is proposed for field-circuit co-simulation, which combines the drift-diffusion equations and Maxwell's equations. The bat algorithm is adopted to match the date sheet of semiconductor to obtain the extracted parameters of physical model. Moreover, with the high-efficiency DGTD solution, the electromagnetic characteristics of field-circuit coupled systems can be analyzed accurately.

articleTitle: Study on Status and Trend of Software Radar Antenna Array
abstract: As the main component of software radar, antenna array needs to have a unified open architecture and interface specification to provide guarantee for new technology implantation and system upgrade and maintenance. The antenna array needs to be able to open a variety of controllable and configurable parameters, to provide a flexible choice of working mode for system, and to have the characteristics of integration, digitalization and common aperture, so as to provide a multi-function and multi-task hardware basis for software radar.

articleTitle: Attenuation Characteristics of Millimeter Wave in Heterogeneous Plasma Generated by DC Arc Discharge
abstract: This paper focuses on DC arc discharge plasma, which has the characteristics of high peak electron density, obvious spatial heterogeneity, and large dimensional scale. The plasma will seriously affect the propagation of millimeter wave, because the collision of electrons with charged particles and neutral particles will absorb a large amount of millimeter wave energy. In the paper, the Coulomb collision and the elastic scattering collision in the plasma are considered comprehensively, and the collision frequency calculation model is established[1]. The layered approximation method is used to divide the non-uniform plasma into multiple layers of approximately uniform plasma, and the computation model of millimeter wave transmission coefficient is derived. The transmission coefficients of 30GHz to 300GHz electromagnetic wave are respectively simulated, the input parameters of plasma are the peak electron density (3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> and 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>), the boundary electron density (1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>) and the length (3m and 1m). The results are shown that when the peak electron density is 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, the transmission coefficients of 30GHz to 100GHz are all less than −30 dB, which means the transmission energy is decreased to 0.1%. As wave frequency is 100–300GHz, the transmission coefficient is from −30dB to −10dB, and the greater the wave frequency, the greater the transmission coefficient. When the peak electron density is 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, the transmission coefficients at the frequency of 30–300GHz are greater than −10dB, which means that the attenuation of electromagnetic wave energy is very weak, that is, it has little effect on the propagation of millimeter waves.

articleTitle: UHF RFID Reader Antenna for Near-Field and Far-Field Operations
abstract: This paper presents a radio frequency identification (RFID) reader antenna designed for near-field and far-field operation. The reader antenna consists of a segmented loop antenna on the periphery and a patch antenna placed inside the loop antenna. The far field of the antenna is circularly polarized (CP), which is achieved by adjusting the patch antenna perturbation and antenna feed position. The simulation results show that the antenna works from 906 to 923 MHz with reflection coefficient less than −10dB, and the axial-ratio bandwidth of less than 3dB is 12MHz (907MHz-919MHz).
